cards.text: Jesus is talking with the Pharisees, a group of strict Jewish religious leaders. They ask Him a big one: when is the kingdom of God going to come? They want a date, friend, and a tracking number.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Pharisees the kingdom of God will come with observable signs.

cards.text: No signs to watch for. And nobody's going to say, 'Look, here it is,' or 'There it is,' like it's a set of car keys somebody finally found in the couch.

cards.question: So where does Jesus tell the Pharisees the kingdom of God is?

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to His disciples. He calls Himself the Son of Man (Luke 22:48), and He tells them a time is coming when they'll long to see one of the days of the Son of Man.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples that when they long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, they will see it.

cards.text: And people will tell them, 'Look, there He is!' or 'Look, here He is!' Friend, that's my group chat every time somebody THINKS they saw a celebrity at the gas station.

cards.question: When people tell them "Look, there He is!" what does Jesus tell the disciples to do?

answers.text: Send one of them to look

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples not to chase those reports. What does He say the Son of Man will be like in His day?

answers.text: Like a quiet knock at night

cards.text: Lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other. Nobody needs a group chat to tell them about THAT.

cards.question: But first, Jesus says, the Son of Man must suffer many things and be ___ by this generation.

cards.text: Then Jesus reaches way back to Noah, the man God told to build the ark (Genesis 6:14). He says just as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the Son of Man.

cards.question: In Noah's day, right up until Noah entered the ark, what were people doing?

cards.text: Then the flood came and destroyed them all. Jesus says it was the same in the days of Lot, Abraham's nephew (Genesis 12:5).

cards.question: Jesus says people in Lot's day were busy buying and selling, planting and building.
Then Lot leaves Sodom. What rains down from heaven that very day?

cards.text: Fire and sulfur, and it destroyed them all. Jesus says it will be just like that on the day the Son of Man is revealed.

cards.question: On that day, Jesus says someone up on the housetop should come down and grab his possessions first.
What does Jesus tell the person out in the field to do on that day?

cards.text: Then Jesus says three words: 'Remember Lot's wife!'

cards.question: Jesus says to remember Lot's wife. Back in Genesis, as she was leaving Sodom, what did she do?

cards.text: She looked back, and she became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26). That's the woman Jesus wants them to remember.

cards.question: Jesus says whoever tries to save his life will ___ it, but whoever loses his life will ___ it.

cards.text: On that night, Jesus says, two people will be in one bed. Same blanket, same fight over who's hogging it.

cards.question: Two people in one bed on that night: one will be ___ and the other left.
Jesus says two women grinding grain together will both be taken.
After all this, the disciples have a question for Jesus. What do they ask?

cards.text: Jesus answers, 'Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.' That's where He leaves it, friend, and so will I.

findings.problem: The card describes the Pharisees as 'a group of strict Jewish religious leaders.' That fact comes from outside the passage, but the card gives no reference for it. The cards that introduce Noah and Lot do give one.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke gives Papa Dorin his own group chat with friends who report celebrity sightings at the gas station. That adds people and a life outside the Dorinverse to his story. He lives on the cookie planet alone, and this isn't a small moment around his bakery. Card 10 calls back to the same group chat. A general comparison, like 'every group chat when somebody THINKS they saw a celebrity,' would keep the joke without adding to his world.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: This story card tells only Genesis 19:26, which is outside the passage. It tells no part of Luke 17 and doesn't move the baker forward through it.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage.

findings.problem: This choice card asks about Genesis 19:26 and cites it, not a verse in the passage. The docs allow facts from outside the passage on cards, with their reference. They don't say whether a choice card can ask about one.
findings.question: Can a choice card ask about a verse outside the passage to explain a reference the passage makes, like 'Remember Lot's wife!'? Or should that background stay on a story card, with every choice card asking about the passage itself?

findings.problem: 'That's where He leaves it' says Jesus stops speaking there. The text doesn't say that. Luke 18:1 goes straight on: 'Then Jesus told them a parable.'

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Most of the story cards in stop 2 (cards 1, 3, 6, 9 and 11) read like a plain narrator. They have no reactions, comparisons, disbelief or self-deprecation. The only real laugh in the stop is the blanket line on card 13. Stop 1 has a joke on almost every story card, so the voice drops off in stop 2.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
